summary: Iteration 2 verifies the new Planning Workspace (Net Worth, Debt, Cash Flow, Insurance, Tax & Estate, Documents, Retirement, Profile) plus regression on auth/dashboard/owners/goals/advisor/crm/PIPEDA/promotion. Backend pytest: 51/51 passing (18 new planning cases parametrized across all 7 collections + 33 regression). Frontend Playwright (solo@compass.ca): login, full sidebar nav (16 testids present), Net Worth list/add/delete round-trip, Cash Flow footer total $4,370 verified, Retirement calculator renders and save persists, Profile income edit persists across reload, Insights/AI/Financial Plan pages render. No blocking bugs.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py planner_scope() returns `read` filter but then post-filters by household_id in Python for GET /api/plan/{collection}. Advisor path with household_id works, but note that advisor without household_id will return the entire org_maple plan_* set — in this iteration no advisor plan_* rows are seeded so it's benign; when advisor planner integration lands, make sure household_id is required for advisor GETs or scope by advisor_id as well.

PUT /api/plan/profile uses body.model_dump() with ProfileInput(extra='allow') — this REPLACES the owner document with only the submitted keys (via repo.update merge). repo.update does field merge (not replace) so this is fine, but validator-free extra='allow' means a malicious/badly-typed client could inject arbitrary fields (e.g. scope override). Consider explicit allowlist for ProfileInput fields.

PlanningItemInput uses extra='allow' with no min-field validation. Clients can POST empty bodies and still get a 200. For v2 consider per-collection schemas or at least requiring `name`/`amount`/`value` depending on collection.

PlanningPage.jsx: the 'edit-{id}' and 'delete-{id}' testids are not namespaced by collection — multiple PlanningPage instances won't collide (only one page is mounted at a time), but reusing just the row id is a bit fragile; `edit-{kind}-{id}` would be safer long-term.
Retirement.jsx and PlanningPage.jsx both duplicate the invalidate(['plan','overview']) pattern. If more pages are added, extract a shared `usePlanMutations(kind)` hook.
